sections.content:
128,230 people

were counted on the census as "elementary construction occupations (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.

People who do this type of work may perform a variety of general labouring and construction duties to assist building, civil engineering and related trades workers in the performance of their tasks not elsewhere classified.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "elementary construction occupations (other)" there were more men than women (97.2% compared with 2.8%).

This means "elementary construction occupations (other)" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary trades and related occupations".

Men made up 97.2% and women made up 2.8% of "elementary construction occupations (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "elementary construction occupations (other)" included:

  • tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out
  • security system installers and repairers
  • metal working production and maintenance fitters

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "elementary construction occupations (other)" had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "elementary construction occupations (other)", 16.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "elementary construction occupations (other)" was 65 years or older.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "elementary construction occupations (other)" included:

  • sports coaches, instructors and officials
  • telephone salespersons
  • animal care services occupations (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "elementary construction occupations (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "elementary construction occupations (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "elementary construction occupations (other)", 8.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (80.7% compared with 19.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (50.6%) than self-employed (49.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Newham, this is in the same region of London.
